subparts.stem: Graph $y = f(x)$ and its inverse function on the same set of axes.
subparts.final_answer: $\text{Graph showing } y = f(x) \text{ and } y = f^{-1}(x) \text{ reflected in } y = x$

mark_breakdown.desc: Sketch $y = f^{-1}(x)$ as the reflection of $y = f(x)$ in the line $y = x$

subparts.solution:
The graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ is a reflection of the graph of $y = f(x)$ in the line $y = x$.
Both curves intersect the line $y = x$ at $(1, 1)$ and $(2, 2)$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The graph of an inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$ is obtained by reflecting the graph of $f(x)$ across the line $y = x$.
step_by_step: Plot $y = 2^{x-1}$ with points $(1, 1)$ and $(2, 2)$ and asymptote $y = 0$.
Reflect the curve across $y = x$ to obtain $y = f^{-1}(x)$, with asymptote $x = 0$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Drawing the asymptotes incorrectly on the wrong axes.

subparts.solution:
$f$ is $y = 2^{x-1}$
$\therefore f^{-1}$ is $x = 2^{y-1}$
$\therefore y - 1 = \log_2 x$
$\therefore y = \log_2 x + 1$
So, $f^{-1}(x) = \log_2 x + 1$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: To find an inverse function algebraically, interchange $x$ and $y$ and solve for $y$ using logarithms.

subparts.stem: State the domain and range of $f(x)$ and $f^{-1}(x)$.
subparts.final_answer: $\text{Domain of } f: \{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R}\}, \text{ Range of } f: \{y \mid y > 0\}; \text{ Domain of } f^{-1}: \{x \mid x > 0\}, \text{ Range of } f^{-1}: \{y \mid y \in \mathbb{R}\}$
subparts.solution:
The domain of $f(x)$ is $\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R}\}$.
The range of $f(x)$ is $\{y \mid y > 0\}$.
The domain of $f^{-1}(x)$ is $\{x \mid x > 0\}$.
The range of $f^{-1}(x)$ is $\{y \mid y \in \mathbb{R}\}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$, and the range of $f^{-1}$ is the domain of $f$.
step_by_step: For $f(x) = 2^{x-1}$, exponential functions are defined for all real numbers: domain is $\mathbb{R}$.
Outputs are strictly positive: range is $y > 0$.
Swap the domain and range for $f^{-1}(x)$: domain is $x > 0$, range is $y \in \mathbb{R}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Swapping the domain and range descriptions incorrectly between $f$ and $f^{-1}$.
